# dsh-codex-mcp
A **DSH host plugin** that runs a loopback-only **Streamable HTTP MCP server** inside the DeepSeek H
arness process, so **Codex can dispatch coding work to DSH** over MCP — no shell wrapper, no per-cal
ocess, so **Codex can dispatch coding work to DSH** over MCP — no shell wrapper, no per-call script.
中文说明 · MIT · zero runtime dependencies
[代码示例省略，未执行]
DSH is still the agent that writes the code. Codex only dispatches the task, reads back a structured
result, and re-runs the acceptance command itself.
## Why a plugin and not a DSH tool
A regular DSH agent tool (`ctx.tools`) is visible only to DSH's own model — Codex cannot see it. To
be callable from another agent, the capability has to leave the process. This plugin therefore:
- starts an HTTP MCP endpoint on `127.0.0.1` when the DSH host loads it, and closes it when the plug

in unloads (`ctx.effect` returns a disposer);
- speaks the MCP Streamable HTTP transport and legacy
JSON-RPC directly — the package deliberately has **no dependencies**, so there is no MCP SDK or `@de

epseek-ai/*` package to resolve inside a profile;
- reuses the DSH install that hosts it: it finds `
@deepseek-ai/dsh`'s `lib/bin.js` next to `resources/app`, or wherever `DSH_APP_ROOT` / `dshCli` poin
epseek-ai/dsh`'s `lib/bin.js` next to `resources/app`, or wherever `DSH_APP_ROOT` / `dshCli` points.
## Features
- **Three MCP tools** — `dsh_env`, `dsh_run`, `dsh_resume`. New sessions and follow-ups both carry t

he session id back to the caller.
- **Structured results** — final answer, `session`, `cwd`, `exit`,
`turn_end`, per-turn token usage, step count, duration; failures also return the stderr tail and a

classified reason.
- **Honest failure** — a call is an MCP error when: it timed out, the child exite
d non-zero, `turn_end` was not `completed`, no `final` event arrived, or the final answer is empty.

DSH's own "I'm done" is never taken at face value by the plugin.
- **Process-tree kill** on timeout

(`taskkill /T /F` on Windows, process group elsewhere), so no orphaned agents.
- **Concurrency cap**

(`maxConcurrentRuns`, default 4) — extra calls fail fast instead of queueing silently.
- **Loopback
-only + Bearer token** — token generated on first start (`32` random bytes, `0600`), compared with s

ha256 + `timingSafeEqual`, path `$DSH_HOME/codex-mcp.token` by default.
- **Bounded NDJSON parsing**

— malformed lines are counted, not fatal; event count, line size and stderr tail are all capped.
-
**Bilingual tool descriptions** (`locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json`) so the calling model reads inst
ructions in its own language.
## Requirements

| DSH | Desktop or CLI install whose `@deepseek-ai/dsh` supports `--profile headless --json` |
| Nod

e | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the host's own Node is used) |
| DSH credentials | a model API key alrea

dy stored in your `~/.dsh` profile (the GUI Models page or the credentials service) |
| DSH profile
| a `headless` profile; the desktop profile rejects `--json` and is managed by the desktop app |

## Tool reference

### `dsh_env()`
No side effects, no tokens spent. Returns JSON: `plugin{name,version,pid,startedAt}`
, `mcp{url,token,tokenFile}`, `dsh{cli,version,profile,dshHome,permissionMode,node,nodeVersion}`, `d
efaults{cwd,timeoutSec}`, `runtime{activeRuns,maxConcurrentRuns}`, and a ready-to-paste `codexConfig
d,timeoutSec}`, `runtime{activeRuns,maxConcurrentRuns}`, and a ready-to-paste `codexConfig` snippet.

### `dsh_run(task, cwd?, timeout_sec?, include_events?)`
Starts a **new** headless session. `task` i
s sent on stdin (no quoting problems, no argv length limit). On success the text result looks like:

### `dsh_resume(session_id, task, cwd?, timeout_sec?)`
Continues an existing session. It must run in
the **same `cwd`** as the original, otherwise DSH refuses before starting (and the plugin says so).
[该节后续省略]
## Security model
- Binds `127.0.0.1` by default. Requests whose peer is not loopback are rejected even if you widen t

he bind, unless you opt in with `allowNonLoopback: true`.
- Every request needs the Bearer token; th
e endpoint returns `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="dsh-codex-mcp"` otherwise. Token comp

arison is constant-time over SHA-256 digests.
- Request bodies are capped at 4 MiB; JSON-RPC batches

are supported; unknown methods get `-32601`.
- The child process runs with `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=dan
ger-full-access` because headless DSH is unattended — it **really can edit files and run commands**
with your user's rights. Always pass a `cwd` inside the project you mean to change, and keep the tok

en out of repositories and screenshots.
- The token file is created with mode `0600`; rotate with `r
egenerateToken: true` (then update Codex's config).
## Limitations

- One plugin instance per host; the endpoint is local-only by design.
- Config or code changes need

a host restart to take effect.
- No streaming progress to the caller — a `dsh_run` call returns when

the task finishes (bounded by `timeout_sec`).
- DSH's sandbox profile decides what the child can do
; this plugin does not add isolation of its own.
